premortem.obituary: It's 12 months on: the bacon strips sat in a saddlebag for six months, degraded from heat and pressure exactly the way C1 describes, and failed to seal on the one ride that mattered — the foil pouch and hard case we built specifically to prevent this didn't stop it, and the review that tanked the rating is the exact '6 months later' story buyer already feared.
premortem.mitigation: Foil-sealed sub-pouch (I2, if fast-followed) plus accelerated-aging validation (40C/70%RH, 6-month equivalent) actually run before launch rather than assumed, and a printed pack/use-by date so buyers can self-check freshness.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Third-party accelerated-aging lab test plus date-coding setup; not sourced this session.

premortem.obituary: A no-name factory photographed our open-case hero shot, copied the slotted hard-case layout within 90 days, and undercut us at roughly 60% of price — the one thing a stranger could actually see in the thumbnail became the one thing that stopped being a differentiator.
premortem.mitigation: Innovaty itself rates I1's prior_art_risk as low precisely because hinged hard cases are generic and easy to copy, so the real defense is speed to market plus a content moat (I3's proof card/video, I4's brand color) that is slower and less obviously worth copying than a case shape; treat the case as a 6-12 month lead, not a permanent moat, and keep iterating.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Rush/expedite fees to compress tooling and shipping lead time to protect the first-mover window; not sourced this session.

premortem.obituary: The new hard case pushed the packaged unit's dimensions a few millimeters over the Small Standard size-tier line, the FBA fee jumped well past our fetched estimate, and the contribution gain from the price increase evaporated into the fee stack.
premortem.mitigation: Lock final packed case+foam+insert dimensions against Amazon's published Small Standard limits during the DFM phase, before tooling sign-off, with explicit slack budget rather than designing to the exact line.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Engineering time for a dimensional-compliance check during the existing DFM phase; not a separate large spend.

premortem.obituary: The Section 301/232 tariff stack on this aluminum-bodied, China-origin tool moved again and landed near the high end of scout's already-stale duty range (near 60%+), and duty alone ate a large slice of an already-thin margin.
premortem.mitigation: Get an actual HTS ruling / licensed customs-broker classification before committing production tooling, hold explicit tariff headroom in the pricing model, and have a fallback (reprice toward $17.99, or evaluate final-assembly diversification outside China) ready if the confirmed rate lands above ~45%.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Customs broker consultation and a formal (or informal) HTS classification opinion; not sourced this session, general market range.

premortem.obituary: Amazon's automated content review flagged the packaging's 'reduces poly-bag film' sustainability line as an unverifiable environmental claim and edited or suppressed the bullet, quietly removing the one extra trust signal we were counting on to offset the missing star rating.
premortem.mitigation: Keep the claim strictly quantitative and file-backed (the BOM weight comparison innovaty already specifies as its verification method), and avoid words like 'eco-friendly' or 'sustainable' per innovaty's own rejected_claims list.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Documentation/compliance-file time only; genuinely low cost.

premortem.obituary: Review velocity stayed too slow to cross the chasm: the blank-rating-tile problem buyer named as fear #3 was never actually fixed by a packaging change, click-through stayed near the bottom of the range, and month-6 share landed at 2% instead of 5%.
premortem.mitigation: Run an early-reviewer seeding program alongside the relaunch and weight the ad budget toward driving the first 50-100 verified reviews fast, since I1-I4 lift add_to_cart and buy (buyer already scores those 0.45/0.55) but do nothing for the click-through gate itself.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Early-reviewer program unit/incentive cost; not sourced this session, general market range.

premortem.obituary: The QR-linked bench-test video and proof card were designed to substitute for the reviews we don't have, but most shoppers on mobile never scanned the code, so the substitute proof never actually reached them and the trust gap buyer named stayed open.
premortem.mitigation: Put the single strongest proof point (e.g. a stated hold-time/mileage claim) directly into a bullet and a secondary image as visible text/graphic, not gated behind the QR scan, so it lands even for shoppers who never scan.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Copywriting and one secondary-image update; low cost, folded into the existing photography line if bundled.

three_sentences_to_founder: Ship the hard case alone first (v1_hero_case): roughly $6,650-$22,200 (base ~$12,050) in tooling, testing, photography and first-ad spend, about $1.6-$7.0/unit landed (base ~$3.27), and it's the one change a stranger can actually see in a 300-pixel thumbnail.

At base assumptions the fee stack alone — 15% referral, ~$4.35 FBA, 30% ad rate — consumes most of a $16.99 price, so contribution margin is thin; hold price near $17-18, keep the case under the FBA size-tier line, and get real ad-rate data before green-lighting anything more, which is why my own call is stretch, not realistic, until that's proven.

Hold I2 (foil pouch), I3 (QR proof card) and I4 (gunmetal finish + red ring) as a near-zero-cost fast-follow once the case is live and reviews start landing, and don't touch I5's valve-core notch until its mandatory ~$1,500 FTO search clears.
